paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. For these people, the line to heaven had gone quiet, and the problem was never on God's end. Isaiah says the LORD's arm is not "too short to save," nor His ear "too dull to hear" (Isaiah 59:1). What stood in the way was their sin, and Isaiah says it plainly: "your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God" (Isaiah 59:2).

Now watch what the people do, because this is the part I love. They stop pointing at "your" and "their" and start saying "we" and "us" (Isaiah 59:9). They say, "our sins testify against us," and they name them out loud (Isaiah 59:12). That's the turn, baker. Honesty about our own sin is where the light starts coming back in, and I'd rather be the stamper who owns his blurry edges than the one who blames the oven!

And then comes the good news, and it's BIG. The LORD saw there was no one to intercede, so "His own arm brought salvation" (Isaiah 59:16). He declares, "The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression" (Isaiah 59:20). His Spirit and His words stay with His people "from now on and forevermore" (Isaiah 59:21). So when you stumble, turn back to Him, because He already did the rescuing and He's not going anywhere. The story isn't over, friend.
